12 THE LIGHTHOUSE KEY
ACT ONE
Scene 1
(Lights rise on a rocky shore. WREN sits on an upturned
boat, scowling at the sea.)
KEEPER. You'll catch your death sitting out
here, miss.
WREN. I don't care. Nobody asked me if I
wanted to come to this horrid island.
KEEPER (gently). Nobody asks the tide, either. Still
it comes.
WREN. That's a stupid thing to say. (She turns
away.) Everything here is grey.
(MRS. HOLLOWAY enters with a lantern.)
MRS. HOLLOWAY. There you are! Supper has been on
the table this half hour.
WREN. I'm not hungry.
MRS HOLLOWAY. Hungry or not, you'll sit.
WREN AND OTIS. We won't!
ALL. Hush!
13
WREN. Who lives in the tower with the red
door?
KEEPER. Nobody, these ten years. The key was
lost the winter Mr. Ashby—
(He stops himself.)
Well. It was lost.
WREN. Lost where?

THE LIGHTHOUSE KEY 14
KEEPER. If I knew that, it wouldn't be lost,
would it? Off you go now. Mind the rocks; they're
slip-
pery after dark.
Scene 2
(The kitchen. OTIS is polishing boots.)
OTIS. You're the new one.
WREN. And you're rude.
OTIS. I'm Otis. I see to the lamps, and the boots, and
15
OTIS (CONT'D)
the keeper's dinner when Mrs. Holloway's busy.
(Grinning.) Which is always.
WREN. I'm Wren. I don't see to anything.
